notes.title: Resident Block Update
notes.notes:
Dear players,

I have updated the resident block sprite so that it will show it's current population and quality of life level. 

If a block population is below 9, or if it's not powered or without jobs, smog stains will appear. 

If population is between 9 and 10, the block will show clean, as it always did. 

And if the population is over 10, nice little plants will appear on the balconies meaning that block can upgrade to a Mega Block. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25673821/a8667326be227701fcd7f4e8ea90b8853daf6b58.png[/img]


I also increased the trees effect, so that you won't need so many of them for blocks to rise over 10 residents.

Finally, a quick fix on "Power to the people" mission, now you will not lose if a power plant falls off the screen. 


Hope you enjoy these changes! 

Have fun!

Fernando

ps. If you have a vote to spare for BalanCity at IndieDB's Top 100 Indies of 2016, please support the game at:

www.indiedb.com/games/balancity

Thanks!

notes.title: Finally, a city building game where utter failure is completely justified
notes.notes:
I've messed up many cities in my term as mayor in any number of city building games, but I've finally found a game in which my dismal failures are completely justified. BalanCity, developed by Fernando Cordoba, finally gives me the perfect excuse for creating a horrible disaster and ruining the lives of my citizens.

In BalanCity, your entire city sits on a giant teeter-totter, meaning that if you build too much one one side, the whole thing starts to tip, and you'll have to hurriedly add to the other side to quickly balance it out:

Residences and offices can be dropped in as little cubes. Provided you've got enough power and mutual support residents need a place to work, and offices need workers the blocks combine into cubes, and the cubes combine into towers. Eventually, your BalanCity will have skyscrapers add elevators so people can reach the upper floors and the height of your city increases by building specialty items like monuments and landmarks.

Not only is it tricky balancing everything, but you'll obviously need to stack new buildings on top of existing ones, and finding a spot for anything that's not perfectly square, like police stations, hospitals, and your mayor's mansion is difficult. In fact, once you've been building for a while, finding room for anything new at all can be a challenge, such as when I had to pile up a police station, fire department, and mayor's mansion on top of each other. Or, when I attempted to find the absolute perfect little spot to build my train station:

Sorry, commuters! As if that weren't enough of a challenge, there are also monsters, aliens, fires, crimes, and even meteor strikes to throw your city into wobbly chaos. One city of mine was struck by a meteor and promptly collapsed. Another time, flying saucers invaded and started abducting all the trees I'd planted to help solve my pollution problems. I've seen my citizens being mugged and have had to quickly build a police station, typically on top of some other building, to arrest the robbers. When fires break out such as when a the police station topples onto a power plant and explodes fire copters need to be dispatched. Provided you can find a spot for it.

It's just a huge hectic nightmare of things constantly going wrong, but as mayor I feel like I can always deflect the blame. "Yes, citizens, I'm aware that several skyscrapers slid into the ocean this morning, and that some of your homes are now in a different part of the city, and are upside-down, and are on fire, but what did you expect to happen when you moved onto a giant see-saw? This is as much your fault as it is mine."

It's almost a relief when something attacks the city to distract everyone from my poor building and planning skills. When a Godzilla-like monster arrived in the wobbly-ass version of San Francisco I was building, I had to quickly add a bunch of military rocket launchers to take him down.

While I think it's cool that my environmentally friendly solar plant was outfitted with a rocket launcher, it didn't do much to quell the tide of destruction the monster caused. Not that my San Francisco was doing particularly well before the irradiated beast showed up. It was a mess of shoddy houses built on the Golden Gate Bridge and offices too far away for citizens to reach. After I managed to dispatch him, everything fell apart anyway:

Like I said, I'm no stranger to having my cities fall into ruin, but at least in BalanCity I don't feel like I'm entirely to blame. The odds are stacked against me in a giant, teetering, wobbly pile.

You can find BalanCity on Steam. It's fun!

notes.title: New Advisors! - October Update
notes.notes:
[h1]October Update - New Advisors, a couple of shortcuts and fixes[/h1]

Hey! It's been a while since the last update but today you will see a couple of new things in the game. 

[b][u]Choose your advisor[/u][/b]

Now you will be able to pick your favorite advisor to assist while you build our city! 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25673821/44bb19a9f0858f9d6ce4f4b4989fe91d5e518158.png[/img]

Apart from SUP, now you can play with [b]Don[/b], [b]Peppy[/b] and [b]Heelaree[/b]. 

Each one has his own power up for your city, Don makes the military more effective, Heelaree makes emergency helicopters faster and Peppy, he just wants to play with you and make unhappy feelings go away. 

[b][u]Scroll and Zoom with the keyboard[/u][/b]

Now you can pan your city view using the directional keys in your keyboard, as well as [b] , [/b] and [b]. [/b] to zoom in and out. 

[b][u]Autosave[/u][/b]

Now the game autosaves Free Build and Scenarios every 10 seconds. Everytime you leave your city, it will be saved so that you can continue building it some other time or if the game crashes. Beware that you cannot leave the game without saving, so it is kind of permadeath of your city if you lost. 



There have been numerous bug fixes and balance tweaks to the game. Please report any bugs you may encounter. 

Have fun! 

Fernando

notes.title: 9-25 More and more Bug Fixes!
notes.notes:
Hey! After some reviews and comments by players I made a couple of fixes and changes to the game mechanics. 

Some of the changes in the game are:

[b]- Block merging now is more tolerant.[/b] It is easier to make mega blocks now.

[b]- Emergency helicopters now do not need to go back to their headquarters. [/b]In a future update I will add the option to build several stations, but now you can place your helis wherever you want and they won't return back home leaving far away from a disaster zone. 

[b]- When you unlock a Special Building, you are not forced anymore to place it.[/b] Now you can continue building whatever you were building and choose when you want to build the Special Building in order to raise your height limit. 

[b]- Mission "Towered Blocks" is the most difficult one and was moved to the last spot in the list.[/b] Also, the inspector is now available as well as trees and terraces that will make that mission a lot easier (some players might find that their progress is messed up, as the last mission will be unlocked and the second and third not, just play mission "Power to the People" again in order to unlock the "Rich & Poor" mission).

I'm glad to read more feedback from players to make BalanCity a better and more enjoyable game! 

yours truly,

Fernando Cordoba

notes.title: 8/24 update!
notes.notes:
Hey! It's been a while but I have been working hard to complete the game. Today's release includes new missions and game configurations. I have also implemented a progression system, so you may see a couple of features locked (don't worry, you can unlock the whole game in the Settings Menu!)

Here's what has been updated:

[list]
[*] New missions! The whole mission pack has been completed. 
[*] Added extra settings to configure Free Build Mode starting conditions such as platform type, gravity strength and a "shantytown" mode.
[*] Added progression system and unlockables. 
[*] Added "Unlock all" and "Reset" buttons to settings menu. 
[*] Added a couple of new music tracks to the scenarios.
[*] Added Windows 64bit build of the game and updated the Mac OSX version (Linux version comes next!)
 
[/list]

The game will be released in a couple of weeks, so feedback and bug reporting is vital at this stage. Hope you enjoy this update and would love to see more gameplay videos! 

See you in the next update!

Fernando

notes.title: 8/2 update!
notes.notes:
Hey! 

The game has been updated with a couple of tweaks to [b]disaster spawn rates[/b]. I've seen many people having trouble with monsters or meteors suddenly destroying their precious work, so I reduced the number of disasters you will face in the first minutes of gameplay.

There is also a new [b]settings screen[/b] in the intro menu. From there you will be able to switch between full screen and windowed mode (does not seem to work properly the first time you click, gotta check on that), mute sound and set the disaster spawn ratio for every type of disaster. Let me know how this work for you and if you think the settings need a little bit of tweaking.

In an upcoming update I will add missions and more tutorial that will cover the things that the regular tutorial does not. For example, mega blocks and skyscrapers.

Don't forget to keep posting feedback! 

See you in the next update!
